Name: Crantzer
Question: In Avengers: Endgame, how did Tony Stark invent time travel in a single evening?
Answer: It wasn’t overnight. Just because the movie skips to Tony at night doesn’t mean it was the same day he had the conversation with Steve, Natasha, and Scott. Tony remarks that he wants to run “one last sim”, implying that he had been running numerous before. Tony also didn’t come up with time travel from scratch. Stark came up with the idea of time travel through a significant head start — Pym Particles. These bad boys are arguably the most advanced piece of technology ever developed by humans (yes, including the Iron Man suits). It was absolutely revolutionary to change how they viewed time and space. It was only through using the template of Hank Pym’s particles that Tony could even scratch the surface of time travel. Without it, he wouldn’t have figured it out.

Question: Who was the most useless character in Avengers: Endgame?
Answer: Korg. Not only was the big rock man useless in the movie, but he actually made things worse. He was one of Thor’s closest friends and helped feed him into a giant rabbit hole of Cheez-Whiz after what happened in Infinity War. Korg is one of those friends who always follows your lead, and thus never actually gives you the help/motivation you need when you’re in a bad place.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would you like if the Darth Jar Jar theory was true?
Answer: Absolutely. The Darth Jar Jar theory would have been one of the greatest twists in cinematic history. And of course, that’s not to mention that it would give both merit and justice to the widely hated character. Jar Jar served no purpose, and it just doesn’t make sense for him to be where he got in the films. Seeing that he was pulling the strings the entire time would’ve done his character justice. That being said, the Darth Jar Jar theory is also certainly plausible. Let’s take a look at some evidence: He’s impossibly skilled at fighting (through pretending to be clumsy), He has been shown to tame animals after waving his hand (a common Jedi mind trick), He can jump impossibly high (Force Jump), He convinced the Senate to give Palpatine emergency powers, His eyes are Sith yellow, And he was identified as a “Jedi” by a Separatist leader.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Star Wars, who’s the most underrated Jedi?
Answer: Definitely Ezra Bridger. Ezra is far more powerful than most people think. He only had around 3–4 years of training under Kanan, and during that period he very quickly gained immense power. In fact, his lightsaber skill became so enhanced that it exceeded that of his master Kanan, a guy who trained in the Jedi Order. But perhaps Ezra’s most notable change was in the Force. For example, he was able to master the very rare ability of mind control. The most advanced of his Force power, however, was his ability to talk to animals. He was able to communicate with Force wolves, and most impressively even controlled purrgil’s — interdimensional space whales who traveled at light speed. Ezra is criminally underrated in terms of power. With due training, he could very well be one of the most powerful Jedi of his time, maybe even surpassing Ahsoka.

Question: What are some major inconsistencies in the MCU that the average viewer doesn’t notice?
Answer: This one’s not really Marvel’s fault, but it is a major inconsistency that happens way often than you think: having the same actors. Here are just a few: Bucky claims to have read The Hobbit, which coincidentally featured Andy Serkis (Ulysses Klaue), Liv Tyler (Betty Ross), Karl Urban (Skurge), Cate Blanchett (Hela), and others as characters in the trilogy. Star Wars (which was confirmed to exist by Steve in The Winter Soldier) has a ton of familiar faces that I am definitely not going to individually list out. Hot Tub Time Machine (referenced in Endgame) also has a fairly familiar face. There are literally hundreds of other examples, but you get the point. Because many of the actors Marvel hires are a-listers, it’s impossible to not have any inconsistencies whenever they reference another big franchise. However, it does make for confusion as to how exactly this works in their universe.
